title: The device catalog
description: Every device model the web installer and MoonDeck offer, one entry per piece of hardware with the state document that sets it up. The rules a schema cannot hold are in README.md; check_devices.py validates against this file and adds them.

name.description: The identifier and the label the picker shows, equal to state.System.deviceModel. At most 31 characters, the device's deviceModel buffer, so it comes back whole.

chip.description: The MCU family, for the picker's chip filter: one of the families moondeck/build/firmwares.py names.

firmwares.description: The firmware variants this hardware runs, each in moondeck/build/firmwares.py; the first is the one the picker selects.

state.description: The state document that sets the device up, the one PATCH /api/state takes. A root key is a top-level module, whose type is not written; a member with a type is a child module, keyed by its name; scalars and arrays are controls.

image.description: The board's picture, our own copy under docs/assets/deviceModels/, named <firmware>-<board> with the chip written dashed.

description.description: One sentence on what the board is, shown in the picker's details.

supported.description: What the firmware drives on this board, shown as solid chips. A new word here needs a module that drives it.

planned.description: What the board has and no module drives yet, shown as dashed chips.

flashBaud.description: The flash baud rate, for a board whose USB bridge needs one other than the default: 921600 from MoonDeck and the command line, 460800 from the web installer.

$patch.description: Its children become the entry's only ones, at this level.

additionalProperties.description: An object is a child module; anything else is a control.
